title: pkix-dane: a sans-IO state machine turns a deleted arm into a hang, not a wrong answer
description:
## What

The first pkix-dane sweep (2026-11-27) reported 19 missed and 13 timeouts
in 237 mutants. The 19 are closed. The 13 timeouts are a class, not a
backlog, and this records why so the next sweep does not re-litigate them.

Eight are deleted match arms of `MxResolution::absorb`, and five are the
counters that advance it (`cname_depth += 1`, `host_index += 1`, and the
`host_index < hosts.len()` comparison in `advance_host`).

## Why they time out rather than fail

`absorb` is a sans-IO state machine: the caller asks `next_step()`, performs
the I/O, and feeds the answer back. Deleting the arm that handles an answer
does not produce a wrong verdict -- it produces a resolution that never
leaves the state it was in, so `next_step()` keeps asking the same question
and the driver loops. Same for a counter that stops advancing: `advance_host`
never reaches the end of the host list.

So the suite detects every one of them, by not finishing. That is the only
verdict available, exactly as for pkix-path's DirStringBytes and
NormalizedIter iterators (PKIX-8d92). Not a coverage gap.

## What is worth doing about it

Nothing, unless the operator can be written out of the code. The pkix-path
case had one such: `Peekable::next_if_eq` removed a reversible comparison
from the mutation space entirely. Nothing equivalent applies to a match arm.

A sweep of this crate should expect ~13 timeouts and read them as caught.
If the count changes, the state machine's shape changed and that is worth
looking at.

## Found by

The pkix-dane sweep, 2026-11-27. Recorded under PKIX-9bzr.
close_reason:
Recorded rather than worked. The 13 timeouts are the only verdict available for a sans-IO state machine: deleting an arm of MxResolution::absorb, or breaking a counter that advances it, produces a resolution that never leaves its state, so next_step() keeps asking the same question and the driver loops. Nothing to chase.

Confirmed by the re-sweep after b01a7843: 237 mutants, 1 missed (the Awaiting::Nothing index bound, equivalent and documented at the site), 13 timeouts unchanged. The 19 real survivors are closed.

Expect ~13 timeouts from this crate. If the count moves, the state machine's shape changed.
